newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rouen grain exports doubled yr/yr in December.
newsitem.headline: Rouen grain exports doubled yr/yr in December.

text.p: Grain exports from the French port of Rouen more than doubled in December from the same period the year before, port officials said on Tuesday.
The port loaded 861,058 tonnes of cereals, mainly wheat, compared with 381,000 tonnes in the last month of 1995.
Italy was the top destination for wheat, with just over 200,000 tonnes out of total wheat exports of 732,571 tonnes.
Egypt was the main world-market destination outside the European Union, with 138,485 tonnes.
Barley exports included 107,487 tonnes for Saudi Arabia.
The surge in exports coincided with a sharp increase in the amount of grain export licences awarded by the European Commission in December.
But exports fell 22 percent on an annual basis in 1996, a year which began with tough curbs on European Union grain exports, provisional port figures show.
Rouen exported 4.987 million tonnes of grain in 1996 compared with 6.385 million tonnes in 1995, port officials said.
